behavioral_effects: Summary.md reports 7 open findings rather than 8; the resolved ENV_VARS drift finding no longer appears.
compatibility_impact: None. Summary.md is regenerated; no schema or contract changed.
limitations: Re-opening a finding now requires a later date or a distinct finding ID, because a closure on the same date always wins. That is a deliberate trade: same-day re-opening is rarer than same-day closing, and requiring a new ID for it is reasonable.
The underlying cause is that change records have date granularity only. A monotonic sequence would order them properly, but adding one is a change-record schema change and therefore a kernel change.
reason: Closing the ENV_VARS drift finding did not remove it from Summary.md. Change records carry a date but no clock time, so several records from one day have no chronology to read, and the summary was falling back to alphabetical ID order — under which the adoption baseline sorted after the closure and its open status won. The bug is that ordering was inferred from something that carries no ordering information.
rollback: git revert this commit. Summary.md then reports resolved findings as open again whenever the closing record's ID sorts before the registering record's on the same date.
security_impact: Positive in effect rather than in mechanism: three high-severity MCP findings and the credential-rotation finding are reported from the same code path, so an ordering bug that hid a closure could equally have hidden one of those.
summary: Resolve finding status by precedence not by ID order
